newsitem.title: USA: Chase has no comment on Lehman rumors.
newsitem.headline: Chase has no comment on Lehman rumors.

text.p: Chase Manhattan Corp spokesman John Stefans said the bank would not comment on market speculation that it might be readying a takeover bid for Lehman Brothers Holdings Inc.
Stefans said the bank would not comment as a matter of policy, which drove Lehman's shares to a new 52-week high.

Lehman shares surged more than four points in late trading as rumors again emerged on Wall Street that the brokerage would receive a buyout offer from Chase, which was also said to be a possible buyer of Lehman in a May round of rumors.
Lehman shares rose 4-4/16 to 49-7/16, a new 52-week high.
Traders said a link-up between the two financial institutions was certainly possible but that today's rumor, first reported on CNBC, was nothing new.

Analyst George Salem of Gerard Klauer Mattison said that the recent wave of mergers in the industry have increased the odds of a marriage between the two financial institutions, especially with few plum brokerages left to choose from.
"Chase is looking for a major investment banking firm," Salem said.

In the past few months, buyouts have rocked the industry, which has been transformed after the barriers that had existed under the Glass Steagall act between U.S. banks, insurance and brokerages were eroded by Congress.
In the past few months, NationsBank agreed to buy Montgomery Securities, Bankers Trust New York Corp will buy Alex. Brown Inc, and Bankamerica said it would buy Robertson Stephens.
